answer: Memory-hard proof-of-work charges computation for each reward claim. Before accepting an umber pigment analysis, violet cultivation plan or sparrow count, verify a puzzle bound to the job, claimant and epoch, then reject reused solutions. N identities need N fresh solutions, consuming memory bandwidth and electricity; renaming accounts cannot reuse that work. Set difficulty so junk claims cost more than their expected payout. This limits cheap aliases, but wealthy operators and specialized hardware retain an advantage.
